headline: Showers fade Saturday; Freeze Watch for parts of southwest Washington Friday night, then a quiet, mild, mostly cloudy week.
summary: As of Thursday evening, a low-pressure center off the coast is moving away to the west and southwest. Showers should taper off tonight, then another batch is expected Friday morning before showers decrease again late Friday afternoon or early evening. The low weakens and moves inland south of the area on Saturday, and conditions dry out. The main hazard is cold: a Freeze Watch is in effect from late Friday night through Saturday morning for the lowlands of Lewis and southern Thurston counties and the Middle Chehalis River Valley. Lows in the Lewis and southern Thurston lowlands are forecast in the upper 20s to around 32 degrees, which can kill crops and sensitive plants, so protect them if needed. Saturday looks partly sunny and dry, with highs in the mid 50s and no rain expected for festivities around the region. From Sunday through the middle or end of next week, a weak upper-level ridge (a zone of higher pressure aloft) builds in. A few weak weather systems may pass through, but forecasters say they are unlikely to bring more than extra clouds. Highs stay in the mid 50s. Forecasters are fairly confident in the drying trend and quiet pattern. There is only a low-confidence hint that wetter weather could return around Nov 6 through 12, which they will keep evaluating.
changes: The big change was the cold: a Freeze Watch for Lewis and southern Thurston lowlands appeared at midday and was expanded in the evening to include the Middle Chehalis River Valley. Forecasters also added a hint of wetter weather around Nov 6 through 12, and the thunderstorm chance noted earlier in the day dropped out as showers faded.
